newsitem.title: CHINA: HK police arrest 14 illegal Vietnamese immigrants.
newsitem.headline: HK police arrest 14 illegal Vietnamese immigrants.

text.p: Hong Kong police arrested 14 illegal immigrants from Vietnam over the weekend, the latest in a series of detentions involving Vietnamese migrants, a police official said on Sunday.
Police arrested 10 men and four women aged 22 to 34 on the outlying Lantau island late on Saturday and early Sunday, a police spokeswoman told Reuters.

The migrants, who claimed to have left Quang Ninh in northern Vietnam on Monday by ship and arrived on Saturday night, said they had paid US$300 each for the voyage that took them to the territory where they wanted to find jobs, she said.
The immigrants would be repatriated, she said.
Last week police arrested 22 illegal Vietnamese immigrants after a massive land, sea and air search prompted by a hoax that hundreds had jumped off a ship in the territory.
Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa said last week he was concerned about the recent influx of Vietnamese.
Hong Kong and Vietnam will soon discuss the feasibility of repatriating illegal Vietnamese immigrants as soon as they are caught, the pro-Beijing Wen Wei Po daily said on Sunday.
Vietnam has insisted the migrants identity should be established before repatriation, the newspaper said.
In recent years, Hong Kong has been repatriating thousands of illegal Vietnamese migrants who were not recognised as genuine refugees.
Repatriation became more frequent in the months approaching Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1. Beijing demanded all detention camps be cleared by the handover.
But some 3,000 Vietnamese are still in the territory, the remnants of a flood of refugees who left Vietnam after the communists won the war there in 1975.
